pr_title: fix(es/fixer): do not strip paren from bin expression
pr_body:
- closes https://github.com/swc-project/swc/issues/2550

## Context:

Original change applied suggested fix in https://github.com/swc-project/swc/issues/2550#issuecomment-952502341 . This made few existing test fails, notably test like https://github.com/swc-project/swc/blob/master/ecmascript/transforms/base/tests/resolver/vercel/next/server/render/1/input.js 

specifically, given input

```
const invalidKeys = Object.keys(data).filter((key) => key !== "revalidate" && key !== "props" && key !== "redirect" && key !== "notFound"
```

creates redundant paren around bin expression like `(key) => (key !== "revalidate" && key !== "props" && key !== "redirect" && key !== "notFound")`.

This PR instead try to skip unwrapping paren if given expression is bin and left hand is object to avoid evaluation fails but preserve existing unwrapping (or not-adding) paren behavior.

I'm not sure if this is feasible approach though, if this works as fix curious if existing wrapping around `seq` could be refactored to skipping unwrap instead.
pr_comments: I used fixture/resolver for the test location, guess I should use fixer's test case itself? Let me try to update to see if I can make changes.
I think it's better to use the fixer test suite itself. `resolver` test can be used, so you don't have to remove it but I think it's better to have one in `fixer.rs`, too

issue_context.title: Unexpectedly strips out parenthesis
issue_context.body:
<!--
If you are using swc at work, please considering adding your company to https://swc.rs/users/
If then, your issue will be fixed more quickly.
-->

**Describe the bug**

Transform output emits code strips out required parenthesis, ends up evaluation fails when try to run code.

**Input code**

```
let isNewPrefsActive = true;
() =>
({
    isNewPrefsActive
} && ({
    a: 1
}));
```

**Config**

```
{
  jsc: {
    target: 'es2017',
    parser: {
      syntax: 'typescript',
    },
  },
  module: {
    type: 'commonjs',
    noInterop: false,
  },
}
```

**Expected behavior**
Emits parse-able code.

**Version**
The version of @swc/core: 1.2.103

**Additional context**

Emitted output:

```
"use strict";
let isNewPrefsActive = true;
()=>{
        isNewPrefsActive
    } && {
        a: 1
    }
;

// Error

  4 |     isNewPrefsActive; 
  5 | }); 
> 6 |  && { 
    |  ^ SyntaxError: Unexpected token (6:1) 
  7 |     a: 1 
  8 | }; 
```
comments: Happy to try to fix this as well, any pointer would be appreciated.

I think adding `e.is_bin()` to https://github.com/swc-project/swc/blob/2febd77c56137406e0fc5467ff3315aebb088f2f/ecmascript/transforms/base/src/fixer.rs#L83-L85 would be enough, but I think there are more types of expressions which is problematic if it's used as a body of an arrow expression.
Thanks, will give it a try. Found this while experimenting swc with our reasonably large codebase, hope (or not?) to find similar cases.
This closed issue has been automatically locked because it had no new activity for a month. If you are running into a similar issue, please create a new issue with the steps to reproduce. Thank you.

review_comments:
Not sure what coverage would like to add - added cases verify 1. if left hand is object, preserve paren 2. if left hand is not object, unwrap regardless of it's binary or not.

Please let me know if test case need to be adjusted, or either additional test case need to be added.
I think test for preserving parenthesis is required, as it ensures that we don't break working code.

Mind elaborate with some pseudo test fixtures? Since change is skipping unwrap, I think these 2 cases covers changed path (first for skip unwrap if condition meets, second to unwrap if doesn't meet new condition). Looks like I may miss some possible paths.
I missed the second one, sorry.
